A map with pins, also called a pin map or marker map, is an interactive map where every location is marked with a clickable pin. Clicking a pin opens details about that place: photos, a description, contact details, a link or a call to action. Pin maps are used for store locators, campus and facility guides, event layouts, service area maps, property listings and any dataset where the useful question is where, not just what. The difference between a pin map and a plain list of addresses is that visitors can see the pattern, filter it, search it and act on it. Pin, marker or point, what is the difference? In practice these three words mean the same thing. Pin describes the classic teardrop shape. Marker is the general term for any symbol placed at a coordinate, whether that is a pin, a circle or a floating icon. Point is the GIS term for the underlying coordinate itself.
